newsitem.title: USA: NBA-SIXERS BRASS UPSET OVER IVERSON ARREST.
newsitem.headline: NBA-SIXERS BRASS UPSET OVER IVERSON ARREST.

text.p: The weekend arrest of Philadelphia 76ers star point guard Allen Iverson on drug possession and weapons charges had team officials in a foul mood on Monday.
"It upsets me and disappoints me," said 76ers owner Pat Croce, who had not spoken with Iverson.
"Everything was on such a positive twist with the new coaches. To have this taint, ... it bothers me, it upsets me, it disappoints me."

The NBA Rookie of the Year and was arrested early Sunday morning in Virginia and charged with misdemeanor possession of less than one-half ounce of marijuana and possession of a weapon while in possession of a controlled substance.

The 22-year-old Iverson was the number one overall selection in the 1996 draft and earned top rookie honours for his outstanding play last season, despite an ego that often made him a lightning rod for controversy.
"We all have made mistakes and this can be corrected, but right now it's not something we can be proud of," said new Sixers coach Larry Brown.
"I've got to wait and see what happens, but this is not very good," said the veteran NBA coach, who joined the Sixers after leaving the Indiana Pacers following the 1996-97 season.
"When you sign a contract and you play in this league, you've got to be responsible," Brown said. "Kids look up to you."
NBA officials would not comment on the incident.
"Until Allen has had his day in court, it would be unfair for us to comment," NBA spokesman Chris Brienza said.

Police said Iverson was a passenger in his own Mercedes, which was stopped for going 93 miles per hour (150 kph) in a 65 mph (105 kph) zone on Interstate 64 in Talleysville, about 20 miles (32 miles) east of Richmond.
When trooper Michael Pierce pulled over the vehicle, he smelled marijuana and discovered the drug and found a .45-calibre handgun on the floorboard of the car.
Iverson was scheduled to be arraigned August 12. Because the marijuana recovered was less than one pound, the weapons infraction likely will be dropped.

"Whether they were his or not, he's a role model," Croce said. "It's an error in judgment. When you make a mistake with who you hang around, it will go right to him first because he is in the public spotlight."
Among the quickest players in the NBA, the six-foot (1.83m) guard was seventh in the league in scoring with 23.5 points per game and 11th in assists with 7.5 per contest.
In April, Iverson scored 40 or more points in five straight games, breaking a rookie scoring record held by Wilt Chamberlain. He became the first Sixer to win the Rookie of the Year award.
